picks.summary: Tonight, we slow down and practice the quiet art of letting go. picks.reason: Zen Buddhist stories and teachings on impermanence and letting go for restful sleep.

picks.title: Sitting Like a Buddha
picks.summary: Where are you located in your body? Most of us, without ever having chosen it, sense ourselves somewhere behind the eyes. Zazen instructions typically bundle two separable practices: disidentifying from thinking, and relocating the self in the belly. Contemporary mindfulness often teaches the first and omits the second. Zen's own instruction is to sit as a buddha rather than in order to become one, trusting a monastic container to do that work silently; outside such a container, this talk suggests, it has to be made explicit. picks.showTitle: Everything Everywhere Daily: History, Science, Geography & More
picks.title: Confucianism
picks.summary:
During the decline of the Zhou Dynasty, warfare and clan violence escalated, threatening the stability of civilization and igniting the Warring States Period. 

Out of the chaos emerged a prolific itinerant teacher offering a path away from bloodshed and political ruin—teachings that would sustain Chinese culture for more than 2,500 years.

His name was Confucius.

Learn more about the enduring power of Confucian philosophy on this episode of Everything Everywhere Daily.
